topic.name: Calculating the Equation of a Normal Line Using Differentiation

question.text: Find where the normal line to the curve $f(x) = 2\sqrt{x}$ at the point $(1,2)$ intersects the $y$-axis.
question.explanation:
Taking the derivative, we have \begin{align*} f'(x) & = \dfrac {\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}x} \left( 2\sqrt{x}\right) \\[3pt] & = \dfrac {\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}x} \left( 2x^{1/2}\right) \\[3pt] & = x^{-1/2} \\[3pt] & = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{x}}. \end{align*}

So the slope of the tangent line is \[ m=f'(1) = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{1}} = 1, \] and therefore the slope of the normal line is \[ m'=-\dfrac{1}{m}=-1. \]

Finally, the equation of the normal line is \begin{align} y - 2 &= -1 ( x - 1) \\ y & = -x +1 +2 \\ y & = -x + 3. \end{align}

Lastly, we find the point of intersection with the $y$-axis by setting $x=0$ and solving the resulting equation. We get \begin{align} y & = -0 + 3\\ y&=3. \end{align}

Therefore, the normal line intersects the $y$-axis at $(0,3).$

question.text: The equation of the normal line to the curve $y = 2x^2$ at the point $(2,8)$ is given by $x+py=q$ where $p$ and $q$ are constants. Find the value of $p+q.$
question.explanation:
Let $f(x)=2x^2.$ First, we compute the derivative: \begin{align*} f'(x) = \dfrac {\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}x} \left( 2x^2\right)=4x \end{align*}

Then, we compute the slope of the tangent at the point $(2, 8):$ \begin{align*} m=f'(2) = 4(2) = 8 \end{align*}

Therefore, the slope of the normal line $m'$ is \[ m'=-\dfrac{1}{m}=-\dfrac{1}{8}. \]

Finally, the equation of the normal line is \begin{align*} y - 8 &= -\dfrac{1}{8} ( x - 2 ) \\[3pt] 8y - 64 & = -x + 2 \\[3pt] x+8y & = 66. \end{align*}

Therefore, $p+q=8+66=74.$

example.title: Determining the Equation of a Normal Line to a Curve at a Point

question.text: Find the equation of the normal line to the curve $y = 4x - \dfrac{2}{x}$ at the point $(-1,-2).$
question.explanation:
Let $f(x)=4x - \dfrac{2}{x}.$ First, we compute the derivative: \begin{align*} f'(x) & = \dfrac {\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}x} \left( 4x - \dfrac{2}{x} \right) \\[5pt] & = \dfrac {\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}x} \left( 4x - 2x^{-1} \right) \\[5pt] & = 4 + 2x^{-2} \\[5pt] & = 4 + \dfrac{2}{x^{2}} \end{align*}

Then, we compute the slope of the tangent at the point $(-1,-2):$ \[ m=f'(-1) = 4 + \dfrac{2}{(-1)^{2}} = 4 + 2 = 6 \]

Therefore, the slope of the normal line is \[ m'=-\dfrac{1}{m}=-\dfrac{1}{6}. \]

Finally, the equation of the normal line is \begin{align*} y - (-2) &= -\dfrac{1}{6}[ x - (-1) ] \\[5pt] -6(y + 2) &= x + 1 \\[5pt] -6y - 12 &= x + 1 \\[5pt] x+\bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{6} \cdot y &= \bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{-13}. \end{align*}
